title: SIEM forwarder & audit schema playbook for private deploys
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines a minimal, audit-friendly SIEM forwarding design, RBAC v2 mappings for evidence export, and network hardening guardrails for Private deployments (VPC-on-cloud and on-prem variants). It targets teams implementing evidence automation (log/trace/export) and customers who must provide SIEM-ready artifacts for third-party compliance review.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: Private deployment control and data plane artifacts (flow logs, application audit events, authz decisions, TLS lifecycle events). Excludes customer app logs unless explicitly routed.
- Intent: Provide reproducible export mappings, example firewall rules and mTLS checklist, an audit log schema that keeps evidence searchable, and an automation pipeline that minimizes manual intervention during a compliance request.

Design goals (why these choices):
- Immutable, verifiable evidence: logs must include non-repudiable identifiers (request_id, principal_id, signature_id) and retention metadata.
- Minimal PI exposure: drop or hash PII at export boundary unless explicit allowlist exists.
- Low operational burden: forwarding should be resilient, use backpressure, and provide replayable archives for forensics.
- Config-driven RBAC: RBAC v2 controls who can trigger evidence exports, read archived bundles, and configure SIEM endpoints.

High-level architecture (ASCII diagram):

+----------------------+     +--------------------+     +----------------+
| Private Deploy Plane  |<--->| Evidence Forwarder  |<--->| Customer SIEM   |
| (control + data)      |     | (buffered, signing) |     | (Splunk/QRadar) |
+----------------------+     +--------------------+     +----------------+
         |                          |   ^  |  
         | app/audit events         |   |  +---- archive -> object store (S3/GCS)
         v                          v   |
    local syslog/                 exporter daemon
    filebeat/otlp                 (tls + mTLS)

Notes: Forwarder has an embedded signer (HSM/KMS integration) that stamps bundles with a key_id and signature for later verification. The forwarder buffers to local object-store when SIEM endpoint is unreachable, and exposes a signed manifest for auditors.

RBAC v2 mapping (recommended roles & resource scopes):
- roles/evidence_reader: read-only access to signed bundles and manifests. Allowed resources: projects/*/evidence/*:read
- roles/evidence_exporter: ability to initiate export jobs (creates signed bundles). Allowed resources: projects/*/evidence:export, projects/*/siem_config:invoke
- roles/siem_admin: manage SIEM connector configs and rotation. Allowed resources: projects/*/siem_config/*:write, kms/keys/*:use_for_signing
- roles/audit_admin: can view audit logs, retention settings, and run replay. Allowed resources: projects/*/audit/*:read, projects/*/evidence/*:replay
- notes on separation: Do not grant evidence_exporter to general SREs. Export jobs must be logged with the initiating principal and reviewed if run ad hoc.

Suggested RBAC v2 policy snippets (human-readable):
- Grant example: "grant roles/evidence_exporter to group:security-operators@redwood.ai on resource projects/acme-corp/evidence"

Audit log schema (canonical fields):
- timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
- event_type (ENUM: authz_decision, authn, api_call, export_request, export_completed, siem_forward, siem_forward_failure, cert_rotate, firewall_change)
- request_id (uuid)
- trace_id (nullable, from tracing headers)
- principal_id (string, format: user:<id> | service:<id>)
- principal_roles (array of strings)
- resource (string, resource path under control plane)
- action (string, e.g., collections/export:start)
- outcome (ENUM: success|failure|denied)
- reason (short string, failure reason or denial code)
- src_ip (CIDR or IP)
- dst_ip (CIDR or IP)
- tcp_ports (list of ports or port ranges, optional)
- tls_info (object serialized as JSON string: {"version","cipher","peer_subject","sni"})
- signature_id (key identifier used to sign the export bundle; empty for normal events)
- retention_policy (string, e.g., P90D)
- obfuscated_fields (list of field names that were hashed or redacted at export boundary)

Example audit event (export_completed) - textual representation:
{
  "timestamp": "2026-01-20T19:04:12Z",
  "event_type": "export_completed",
  "request_id": "b7f3a5e2-9a1e-4f3b-a2c7-0d9f1c4d3e6a",
  "principal_id": "service:evidence-batcher",
  "resource": "projects/acme-corp/evidence/exports/2026-01-20-19-04",
  "action": "exports/bundle:create",
  "outcome": "success",
  "signature_id": "kms-key-02:sign-v1",
  "retention_policy": "P365D"
}

PII handling and redaction model:
- Default: PII fields (email, ssn, phone) are hashed with salt at export boundary. Salt is per-customer and stored in KMS-protected secret.
- Allowlist: Customers can opt-in to include full PII in bundles; this requires a signed policy request and must be logged under event_type=export_request with justification.

Evidence automation pipeline (steps):
1) Trigger: scheduled or manual export request (RBAC-checked).
2) Snapshot: collector queries control-plane stores for events/flows in requested window.
3) Normalize: events transformed to canonical schema, PII hashed per policy.
4) Bundle: create compressed archive with manifest.json and signed_manifest.sig.
5) Store: push to archival object store (S3/GCS) with server-side encryption and immutability flags where supported.
6) Forward: forwarder attempts live SIEM POST over mutual-TLS (client certs). On failure, it enqueues and retries with exponential backoff to local disk.
7) Verify: on successful forward, mark manifest as forwarded and emit export_completed audit event with signature_id.
8) Replay API: allow auditors to pull signed bundles and verify signatures via KMS public key.

SIEM export contract (HTTP + mTLS):
- Endpoint: POST /ingest/evidence/batch
- Auth: mutual TLS with client cert commonName=<forwarder-id>, server cert validated. TLS 1.2+ recommended, prefer 1.3.
- Payload: multipart/related
  - part 0: manifest.json (metadata list of files, checksums, signature_id)
  - part 1: bundle.tar.gz (binary)
  - part 2: signed_manifest.sig (detached signature)
- Forwarder behavior: include X-Forwarder-Id header and X-Forwarder-Sent-At (ISO8601). Retries: 5 attempts, exponential backoff, 2m max interval.

Firewall & VPC pattern recommendations (minimal practical set):
- Control plane subnets (private): only allow egress to forwarder endpoints and KMS endpoints via egress proxy; deny inbound except from load-balancer IPs.
- Forwarder subnet: allow outbound TCP 443 to SIEM collector IPs; allow outbound to object store endpoints (S3/GCS). Allow inbound only for management IPs (ops corpnet) on SSH via bastion.
- Firewall rules (example, cloud-ACL style):
  - deny all ingress to control-plane-* except ELB/ALB health check ranges
  - allow egress control-plane-* -> kms.*:443 (TLS)
  - allow forwarder-* -> siem.collector.corp:443 (mTLS)
  - allow forwarder-* -> s3.amazonaws.com:443 (storage)
  - restrictive CIDR lists for ops management range only

mTLS lifecycle checklist (operational):
- Certificate issuance: use short-lived client certs (30d recommended) from internal PKI; record cert_id in audit events.
- Rotation: stagger cert rollouts across forwarders; rotate one batch at a time; do not rotate all certs at once.
- Revocation: support CRL/OCSP checks in SIEM collector. If not available, maintain a denylist service and include denial checks in forwarder.
- Test: quarterly simulated failover where collector rejects current cert to validate queued replays and recovery.

Operational runbooks (quick actions):
- If SIEM forwarder is failing (high siem_forward_failure counts):
  1) Check forwarder logs for TLS handshake failure -> verify certificate validity and trust chain.
  2) If network timeout -> confirm firewall egress rules and outbound NAT.
  3) If rate-limited -> fall back to batch archive path and notify security-operators.
  4) Always run signature verification on any archived bundle prior to handing to auditors.

Evidence verification steps for auditors:
- Pull signed_manifest.sig and manifest.json.
- Verify signature against KMS public key provided via secure channel.
- Check checksums in manifest match files in bundle.tar.gz.
- Confirm export_completed event exists in audit index for the bundle request_id.

Appendix: quick checklist (for releases):
- [ ] RBAC policies created: evidence_reader/exporter/siem_admin
- [ ] Forwarder config tested in staging with mTLS to collector shim
- [ ] KMS signing key policy reviewed and rotated if > 90 days old
- [ ] S3/GCS object lifecycle and immutability configured (WORM if required)
- [ ] Automated replay API endpoint tested with auditor key
- [ ] Smoke test: generate export, verify signature, push to SIEM, verify receipt

Open questions / decisions to track: 
- Do we require WORM/immutability by default for all customers or opt-in? (security ops)
- Preferred cadence for certificate rotation across large fleets (ops + infra)
- Storage of salts for PII hashing for customers with multi-region redundancy (compliance team)

Contact and ownership:
- Primary author: Aisha Raman (eng-private-deployments)
- Reviewers: Priya Nair (security), Marco Chen (sre), Evan Morales (platform infra)

This doc is a working playbook; implementation details (endpoints, bucket names, keys) should be moved to an environment-specific secrets repo and referenced from the forwarder config.
